label: Count the squared terms
subgoals: Check whether both variables are squared
One squared variable means a parabola
Two squared variables narrow it to three conics

visual.title: One equation, several curves
visual.caption: Raise the cross term B and the conic turns without changing kind. A and C decide the kind through their signs and the discriminant, and when one squared term vanishes the curve is a pair of parallel lines rather than a parabola.

predict.question: Keep A and C positive and raise the cross term B. Which type can B alone produce?
options: None: B only rotates the ellipse
predict.explain: B adds a rotation. The discriminant is B squared minus 4AC, and with A and C positive 4AC wins unless the terms balance exactly.

label: Compare the coefficients
subgoals: Unequal coefficients with the same sign mean an ellipse
Do not confuse a scaled circle with an ellipse

label: Check the signs
subgoals: Same signs rule out a hyperbola
